★★★ A HAND-WRITTEN INDIRECT BRANCH THROUGH AN INTERIOR LABEL'S ADDRESS — the x86_64 half of D-ASM-INTERIOR-LABELS-NOT-ADDRESSABLE-AT-AN-OFFSET, and with it D-ASM-INDIRECT-BRANCH-SUCCESSOR-SET-UNSTATED. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-13: pe64 exits 42 on Windows, elf64 exits 42 on Linux.

★★★ WHAT THE CAPABILITY ACTUALLY WAS. `leaq Lwin, %rax` lowers to the operand pair `[SymbolRef, BlockRef]` — BYTE-FOR-BYTE the shape `mir_to_lir.cpp`'s `lowerBlockAddress` already emitted for C's `&&label`, and the x86_64 target already declared the matching `lea` variant `{"operandKinds": ["symbol","blockref"], "width": 64}`. The encoder reads the trailing BlockRef, records a `BlockSymPatch`, and `assemble()` binds the synthetic symbol to that block's byte offset; the linker gives it an interior VA. So the front-end wiring is the whole change: no new operand kind, no new relocation kind, no encoder edit, no linker edit.

★★ TWO ADDRESSES ARE TAKEN BECAUSE ONE PROVES NOTHING. With a single address-taken label the branch has exactly one possible destination and a build that ignored the register would still exit 42. Here the derived successor set has TWO members and `Lfail` is laid out FIRST, so: ✔MEASURED by rebuilding this same file with `leaq Lwin` changed to `leaq Lfail` — exit 1. The branch follows the address that was loaded, not the layout.

★★ AND IT SURFACED A REAL DEFECT THAT WAS NOT ASSEMBLY'S. Writing the swapped variant made the SAME label's address be taken twice, which failed to LINK: `K_SymbolUndefined: symbol #N is declared more than once`. ✔MEASURED that C had it identically — `void *a = &&L; void *b = &&L;` did not compile. `mintBlockSymbol` is memoized per block, so N block-address sites are N patches carrying ONE SymbolId, and `assemble()` pushed one `SyntheticBlockSymbol` per PATCH rather than per SYMBOL. The jump-table arm of the pipeline already had the guard; its encoder-driven sibling did not — one path right while its twin was wrong, which is a recurring shape here. Fixed at the source in `assemble()`, so both languages get it, and pinned in the unit tier.

★★ THE REFUSAL IS STILL REACHABLE, WHICH IS HOW A DERIVABILITY-KEYED GATE IS SUPPOSED TO AGE. `jmp *%rax` in a function with NO address-taken label is still refused, naming the missing binding rather than the instruction — the refusal site was never edited by this cycle, its condition simply stopped holding for files like this one. That negative arm is pinned in `tests/asm/test_asm_text_to_lir.cpp`.

⚠ THE `(%rip)` SPELLING IS NOT WRITTEN HERE, AND THE REASON IS NAMED. gcc -S writes `leaq .L4(%rip), %rax`, but the x86_64 target declares no `rip` register at all (✔MEASURED: `unknown register 'rip' — this target declares no register by that name`), so the RIP-relative SPELLING is blocked on a target-vocabulary decision — an instruction-pointer register must not be allocatable — that is not this row's. The bare-symbol form written here reaches the identical `lea [symbol…]` lowering, which emits RIP-relative bytes anyway. Anchored: D-ASM-RIP-RELATIVE-SPELLING-NEEDS-AN-IP-REGISTER.

⚠ NO arm64 LEG HERE, DELIBERATELY: this file is x86_64 AT&T assembly and names x86 registers, so it is not portable text. The arm64 half is its sibling `asm_arm64_jump_table_and_data_readback`, which additionally covers the data-defined jump table this dialect cannot yet spell.

★★ RED-ON-DISABLE, i.e. what breaks this fixture and how: swap `leaq Lwin` for `leaq Lfail` (exit 1); delete either `leaq` (the successor set shrinks, and deleting the `Lwin` one refuses because nothing binds the branch's target); drop the `jmp` row's `jmp_indirect` candidate (the star operand has no arm to elect); bind the interior symbol to the function start (control re-enters `main`); make the lowering emit `[symbol]` instead of `[symbol, blockref]` (the symbol is never bound to a byte offset — pinned as a target mutant in the unit tier); remove `.type main, @function` (`Lfail`/`Lwin` stop being blocks of `main` and become functions, and the address-of crosses a function boundary, which is refused).

★ THE `release` ARM, SCOPED HONESTLY. At the `encode` tier no MIR module exists, so the optimizer, the register allocator and calling-convention materialization never run — this arm does NOT witness the optimizer and cannot. It pins the narrower fact that `--config=release` still produces a working binary from assembly.
